raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-STP-YouthEmployment",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Training institutions lack adequate equipment, infrastructure and staff, limiting the quality and scale of technical training.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Allocate funds for equipment upgrades, refurbish facilities, recruit qualified instructors and provide continuous professional development.",
      "evidence": "capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps (Section 12)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Curricula may not match employer needs, leading to skills mismatches and low graduate employability.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish regular employer advisory panels, embed employer‑driven competency standards in curricula, and monitor placement outcomes.",
      "evidence": "most firms perceive that the education and training systems do not adequately prepare youth (Section 11)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Floods, storms and landslides could damage training facilities and disrupt program delivery.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate climate‑resilient design in renovations and new construction, and develop contingency plans for temporary relocation of activities.",
      "evidence": "STP is vulnerable to coastal and riparian floods, severe storms, landslides (Section 4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Delays in financial reporting and internal audits may hinder timely disbursements and compliance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint an experienced accountant, customize accounting software for real‑time reporting, and enforce strict audit timelines.",
      "evidence": "delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports; internal audit reviews not timely (Section 56)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Weak coordination between AFAP and ministries could slow procurement of goods and services.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Create joint procurement task‑forces with clear SOPs and shared timelines, and hold weekly coordination meetings.",
      "evidence": "ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration is key for timely procurement (Section 57)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment affecting especially female trainees and interns.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Hire dedicated GBV/SEA specialists, implement strict code of conduct, provide safe reporting channels and conduct regular awareness trainings.",
      "evidence": "require hiring Environmental Specialist with SEA/SH expertise; risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (Legal covenants)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Beneficiary selection may exclude marginalized groups or be captured by elites, undermining equity goals.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use transparent, data‑driven targeting from the Unique Social Registry, and establish independent oversight of selection processes.",
      "evidence": "risks of exclusion, especially for marginalized groups, if benefits not equitably distributed (Section 58)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "The new labor market information system may not become fully functional, limiting data‑driven employment services.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt a phased rollout with pilot testing, allocate dedicated IT staff, and secure vendor support for system maintenance.",
      "evidence": "Employment Observatory never fully operationalized; new system may not be operational (Sections 32‑33)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "CERC may not be activated promptly during a crisis, delaying reallocation of funds to vulnerable beneficiaries.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Finalize the CERC manual before effectiveness, train staff on activation procedures, and conduct tabletop simulations annually.",
      "evidence": "CERC manual to be prepared after effectiveness; staff orientation required (Section 47)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Insufficient partnerships with overseas employers could limit labor‑mobility opportunities for youth.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Negotiate MoUs with destination‑country employers, leverage CPLP networks, and showcase qualified candidates through the Employability Portal.",
      "evidence": "explore partnerships with relevant overseas employers to advertise opportunities (Section 34)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Limited grant and scholarship budgets may fall short of the target numbers of beneficiaries.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Monitor disbursement pace quarterly, re‑prioritize allocations if needed, and seek supplemental donor contributions.",
      "evidence": "project finances 0.00 financing gap but grant amounts limited; risk of not meeting 1,000 scholarships (Section 44)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Cultural and time‑poverty constraints may prevent women from reaching the 50 % participation target.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide childcare services at training sites, schedule flexible class times, and conduct gender‑sensitive outreach through women’s associations.",
      "evidence": "women face higher poverty, lower labor participation; project aims 50 % women but barriers exist (Sections 9, 23)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Private sector firms may not actively engage in Workforce Development Committees, reducing relevance of training programs.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Offer incentives such as partial compensation for training slots and public recognition for participating firms.",
      "evidence": "Workforce Development Committees bring together private sector employers; participation may be limited (Section 27)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Logistical challenges of delivering equipment and staff to Príncipe could delay construction of the new training centre.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a detailed logistics plan, secure local transport contracts early, and build buffer time into the construction schedule.",
      "evidence": "Príncipe is 170 km away, geographically isolated, with limited skilled workers (Section 1)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Weak monitoring and evaluation data quality could impede learning and evidence‑based adjustments.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement standardized data collection tools, train staff on M&E protocols, and conduct periodic data quality audits.",
      "evidence": "monitoring includes spot checks; risk of weak data if not properly managed (Section 51)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Training institutions lack adequate equipment, infrastructure and staff, limiting the quality and scale of technical training.
risks.mitigation: Allocate funds for equipment upgrades, refurbish facilities, recruit qualified instructors and provide continuous professional development.
risks.evidence: capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps (Section 12).

risks.description: Curricula may not match employer needs, leading to skills mismatches and low graduate employability.
risks.mitigation: Establish regular employer advisory panels, embed employer‑driven competency standards in curricula, and monitor placement outcomes.
risks.evidence: most firms perceive that the education and training systems do not adequately prepare youth (Section 11).

risks.description: Floods, storms and landslides could damage training facilities and disrupt program delivery.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilient design in renovations and new construction, and develop contingency plans for temporary relocation of activities.
risks.evidence: STP is vulnerable to coastal and riparian floods, severe storms, landslides (Section 4).

risks.description: Delays in financial reporting and internal audits may hinder timely disbursements and compliance.
risks.mitigation: Appoint an experienced accountant, customize accounting software for real‑time reporting, and enforce strict audit timelines.
risks.evidence: delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports; internal audit reviews not timely (Section 56).

risks.description: Weak coordination between AFAP and ministries could slow procurement of goods and services.
risks.mitigation: Create joint procurement task‑forces with clear SOPs and shared timelines, and hold weekly coordination meetings.
risks.evidence: ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration is key for timely procurement (Section 57).

risks.description: Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment affecting especially female trainees and interns.
risks.mitigation: Hire dedicated GBV/SEA specialists, implement strict code of conduct, provide safe reporting channels and conduct regular awareness trainings.
risks.evidence: require hiring Environmental Specialist with SEA/SH expertise; risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (Legal covenants).

risks.description: Beneficiary selection may exclude marginalized groups or be captured by elites, undermining equity goals.
risks.mitigation: Use transparent, data‑driven targeting from the Unique Social Registry, and establish independent oversight of selection processes.
risks.evidence: risks of exclusion, especially for marginalized groups, if benefits not equitably distributed (Section 58).

risks.description: The new labor market information system may not become fully functional, limiting data‑driven employment services.
risks.mitigation: Adopt a phased rollout with pilot testing, allocate dedicated IT staff, and secure vendor support for system maintenance.
risks.evidence: Employment Observatory never fully operationalized; new system may not be operational (Sections 32‑33).

risks.description: CERC may not be activated promptly during a crisis, delaying reallocation of funds to vulnerable beneficiaries.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the CERC manual before effectiveness, train staff on activation procedures, and conduct tabletop simulations annually.
risks.evidence: CERC manual to be prepared after effectiveness; staff orientation required (Section 47).

risks.description: Insufficient partnerships with overseas employers could limit labor‑mobility opportunities for youth.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate MoUs with destination‑country employers, leverage CPLP networks, and showcase qualified candidates through the Employability Portal.
risks.evidence: explore partnerships with relevant overseas employers to advertise opportunities (Section 34).

risks.description: Limited grant and scholarship budgets may fall short of the target numbers of beneficiaries.
risks.mitigation: Monitor disbursement pace quarterly, re‑prioritize allocations if needed, and seek supplemental donor contributions.
risks.evidence: project finances 0.00 financing gap but grant amounts limited; risk of not meeting 1,000 scholarships (Section 44).

risks.description: Cultural and time‑poverty constraints may prevent women from reaching the 50 % participation target.
risks.mitigation: Provide childcare services at training sites, schedule flexible class times, and conduct gender‑sensitive outreach through women’s associations.
risks.evidence: women face higher poverty, lower labor participation; project aims 50 % women but barriers exist (Sections 9, 23).

risks.description: Private sector firms may not actively engage in Workforce Development Committees, reducing relevance of training programs.
risks.mitigation: Offer incentives such as partial compensation for training slots and public recognition for participating firms.
risks.evidence: Workforce Development Committees bring together private sector employers; participation may be limited (Section 27).

risks.description: Logistical challenges of delivering equipment and staff to Príncipe could delay construction of the new training centre.
risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed logistics plan, secure local transport contracts early, and build buffer time into the construction schedule.
risks.evidence: Príncipe is 170 km away, geographically isolated, with limited skilled workers (Section 1).

risks.description: Weak monitoring and evaluation data quality could impede learning and evidence‑based adjustments.
risks.mitigation: Implement standardized data collection tools, train staff on M&E protocols, and conduct periodic data quality audits.
risks.evidence: monitoring includes spot checks; risk of weak data if not properly managed (Section 51).
